subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for an armoured convoy hauler with a sealed cargo pod, low-poly cyberpunk style, built as a static model using basic part, extrude, and lathe geometry in model space.

I'm sketching out dimensions: a chassis roughly 9m long with a front cab, a capsule-shaped lathed cargo pod with sealed bands, plus six wheels, armour plating, a roof turret, light bars, exhaust stacks, antenna, searchlights, and SVG decals for hazard stripes and warning text, all kept grounded at y=0.

Now I'm working out the helper for placing geometry with paints and colors, setting wheel rotation axes along X, and shaping the cab with a slanted, tilted windshield box.

Still defining cab geometry...

Working out the decorative bands around the pod, trying to size the ring geometry so it wraps cleanly around the octagonal cross-section without poking through the vertices.

For surface details, I'm figuring out placement of a mounted label plate with a textured decal, positioning it to bridge slightly into the pod's flat side so it reads as physically attached rather than floating.

I'm now working out the texture plane's orientation—tracing axis mappings to figure out which direction is "right" on the decal when viewed from the vehicle's side, since the plane's local coordinate system doesn't automatically align with the viewer's perspective.

Now I'm planning the set of textures needed: a "SEALED CARGO 7-K" hazard-pattern pod label with neon biohazard styling, a yellow/black diagonal hazard stripe pattern for the bumper and skirt, a cyan glow strip for the headlight visor, a corporate emblem for the cab doors, and a windshield HUD overlay texture.

Still working out the wheel geometry — six wheels across three axles, with tire cylinders, metal hubcaps, and a thin neon cyan ring glowing beneath each cap, including dual rear wheels per side.

Now I'm sizing the chassis so the wide-stance wheels extend beyond the 2.4-wide cab, pushing total vehicle width to around 3.2, and sketching boxy wheel arches and sloped mudguards to cover them, plus considering angled side-skirt armor plates along the pod cradle.

For the skirts, I'm placing hazard-textured boxes between the wheels and designing a wedge-shaped front ram bumper using an extruded side profile that tapers up toward the cab front, topped with additional hazard-striped texture bands.

Now I'm adding a grill with glowing slits and push bars up front, then a roof turret with a cylindrical base, a boxy housing, and twin forward-facing barrel rods, plus sensor dome spheres and a glowing front light bar. I'm also positioning exhaust stacks as paired cylinders behind the cab, roughly mirrored on either side.

Checking clearances now — stacks sit at z 2.1, clear of the pod's shrinking nose radius which ends around 1.9. I'm planning fuel tank cylinders along the chassis sides, positioned to avoid overlapping the wheel axles front and back.

Now I'm placing three pod cradle saddles underneath the pod with glowing containment latches, plus the main chassis beam box, and designing the rear bumper with glowing red taillights, a rear guard, and towing hooks near the back of the chassis.

I'm also adding ribbed band rings along the pod's length for armor, with steel coloring and alternating glow strips along the top spine, plus a circular vault-style sealing door disc at the rear nose end.

Then I'm planning cab details: thin antenna rods with glowing tips, mirror boxes on arms, and dark glass side window panels sized to the cab's width.

For the windshield, I'm calculating the tilt angle of the cab's sloped front (about 33.7° backward) so the glass box aligns correctly along that slope's normal direction.

For the windshield I'll skip text and go with scan lines, reflection streaks, and a cyan tint with a slight glow for the cyberpunk feel. I'm adding underglow strips in cyan and magenta along the chassis sides near the bottom, and placing glowing white-cyan headlight boxes on the cab's front lower bumper.

Now I'm working through the headlight and bumper geometry, adjusting the wedge outline so the sloped bumper doesn't overlap or swallow the headlight bars near the front of the cab.

I'm also building the cab's extrusion profile as a sequence of points, making sure the outline stays non-self-intersecting while shaping the slope from the top of the bumper up to the windshield line, checking the angle and normal direction of that sloped edge.

Now I'm placing the windshield centered along that slope, offsetting slightly by the normal, and sizing it with margins so it sits cleanly within the slanted panel. I'm sorting out dimensions—cab width, overall thickness, windshield width—then picking a cyberpunk color palette for the cab: dark gunmetal with magenta, cyan, and yellow hazard accents instead of a plain metal tone.

I'm defining paint textures for the hull and pod using a panelled material with a base hex color, panel size, and rivet pitch, then checking texel density against the paint resolution to see if seam lines at 2.5mm will actually be visible or get lost sub-pixel at a 2048 paint size.

Given seams risk vanishing, I'm switching to a custom paint function that defines panel lines directly from surface coordinates, adding 1.5-2cm dark seam lines along the dominant UV axis, plus grime/dust blending near the lower parts of the hull and lighter tones on upward-facing surfaces, pulling in noise, mix, and smoothstep utilities. I'm now setting up the base hull and dark accent color variables.

Filling out the rest of the palette (plate, magenta/cyan accents, hazard yellow, rubber, steel, glass, red, purple), then planning the painted materials for cab, pod, and chassis, and sketching out part-count goals with reusable box/cylinder helper functions and mirrored loops for symmetry. Writing texture setup for pod labels and other SVG-based decals...

I still need a windshield texture, a vault wheel design for the circular hatch, and a rear plate reading "CONVOY 03." I'm also considering a neon roof banner reading "NEON" to round out the full texture set to six.

I'm debating a small cyberpunk billboard above the cab reading "AEGIS" in magenta glow, but it's adding complexity for little payoff, so I'll likely skip it and keep things cheap. For glow, I'll apply it selectively to textured parts like the glass, using a moderate strength so the colors bleed through without overpowering everything, keeping each glowing part on a single standard material. Now I'm building the tire geometry as a cylinder for the wheel details.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Checking wheel positions at the three z-offsets, I notice the cab and wheels overlap slightly at x=1.05 versus 1.15, so I'm adjusting wheel x to 1.42 with tire width 0.55, giving a span of 1.145 to 1.695 that clears the cab properly.

Now I'm positioning axle rods as visible cylinders beneath the chassis, sitting at y 0.55 within the lower beam, with fenders built as armoured arches using a flat top box and outer lip detail.

For the cab sides, I'm extruding angled armor plates following a side-profile polygon, placed symmetrically at x ±1.2, with an accent stripe sprite and a recessed window plane for the door.

Working out the extrusion axes for the outline thickness, then moving to the pod geometry—defining it as a lathed octagon shape along the z-axis, and figuring out where the top shimmer strip should sit based on whether the octagon has a vertex or flat face at the top.

Also need glow lock boxes on band tops plus a rear vault. Checking the pod side label plates against the flat position - widening to .2 fixes the gap issue, centered at x 1.25. Now working out band z-positions along the pod relative to the label plate span and the front rounding of the pod.

Placing bands at z -3.7, -3.2, 0.5, and 1.0, matching up against the outline and label plate bounds. Then I'm positioning cradle saddles under the pod at roughly z -3.0, -1.2, 0.2, sized to match the pod's bottom curvature.

Now I'm detailing the rear structure: a bumper box with taillights near the chassis end, the pod nose cutoff, and a thin dark ring (vault detail) placed near z -4.33 with a small radius, oriented along the z-axis near the rear plane.

Then I'm switching to the gun turret: a cylindrical base at the top, a small body box above it, and two parallel barrels extending forward from the body, positioned symmetrically along x with a muzzle glow at the tips, plus a sensor sphere mounted at the top.

I'm checking for overlaps between the turret and the roof lightbar - realizing their z-positions conflict since both sit near the cab roof and front pod area, so I'm nudging the turret back slightly to clear the collision.

I'm sketching out cab roof accessories: antenna rods with glowing tips plus a small satellite dish built from a lathe profile, working out an outline shape that properly closes.

I decide skipping the dish is simpler and swapping in a box-shaped sensor array instead, then start positioning exhaust stacks behind the cab at x ±1.0, checking clearances against the pod and turret base, and adding cone caps with glowing orange rings on top. Now I'm thinking about where to place the fuel tanks, considering x positions around ±1.25.

I check tank placement against the wheel positions to avoid collisions, settling on cylinders with ten sides positioned at x ±1.3, centered around y 0.9, verifying they clear the pod geometry above, and I'm leaning toward a dark purple accent color with a glowing stripe band for the tanks.

Adding mirrors and underglow strips...

Now I'm thinking through the front bumper details—adding spike cones for a cyberpunk look and a thin hazard strip across the wedge top.

Then I'm positioning the headlight glow boxes near the cab front, flanking a dark grill box with glow slits in between.

Checking the cab geometry for consistency: lower front panel height, headlight placement, door handles, and an accent stripe along the armor plate's bottom edge, verifying positions stay flush without clipping through adjacent parts.

Now I'm placing cab roof intake boxes and considering whether to add small beacon lights on the pod ends or rear bumper, deciding these might be unnecessary detail. I'm also reconsidering the side skirts near the rear axles, adjusting their z-range so they fit between the wheel positions without overlapping.

I'll add ammo crates at the chassis sides between the wheel and tank area, sizing them to fit the chassis width with hazard texture and stripes on all faces. For the pod, I'm thinking about adding angled armor fins or shield plates on the front and rear, though I'll skip a shoulder-mounted nose shield and instead consider a simple arch or rib detail on top.

I'm skipping the angled armor wedges on the pod's upper corners since positioning them correctly on the octagonal face is too risky -- the label plates, bands, and top spine already look good enough. I'll also skip a top ridge rail and a visible cab number, and move on to adding red rear taillight boxes.

Now I'm placing the taillight glow and emblem plate, then writing the SVG texture for a hazard pattern with slanted yellow-and-black warning stripes.

Writing the cargo label texture...

GLASS also gets thin cyan HUD lines and a tiny "CONVOY LINK" label; PLATE is a simple white license-plate style with "CV-03" in black. That rounds out six total assets, and now I'm writing the paint function that maps 3D normals to UV coordinates for texturing each face.

Still defining material colors...

I'm listing the needed imports from the builder kit, including the glow module path, and noting I should avoid naming conflicts with the OutlinePoint type.

Now I'm sketching the builder API shape—lathe and extrude helper options, bevel settings, and a decal plane helper for applying textures to flat surfaces—before writing the actual construction code for the convoy hauler model.

I'm placing the windshield as a rotated textured box, positioning the wheels along the Z-axis, and adding mudflap boxes behind each wheel.

Now I'm defining the rear axles as cylinders rotated along the X-axis, checking that the front axle sits properly under the cab, and verifying the wheel geometry doesn't leave a gap floating above the ground due to the cylinder's radial vertex positioning.

I'll adjust the wheel y-position to .54 so the lowest vertices touch the floor alongside the chassis and bumper. Now I'm planning the remaining elements: antenna height, exhaust glow cylinders, side window and mirror loops, and the light bar made of two colored boxes (magenta and cyan) mounted flat against the roof's non-sloped section.

Adding more parts: intake boxes, pod sign plates, fuel tank bands, a loop of alternating-colored side marker lights positioned to avoid clashing with the wheels, front fenders, and small cone-shaped spikes angled forward near the bumper.

Finishing the layout: positioning the rear bumper box, taillights, and license plate at the back of the vehicle, with the vault ring placed clear of the bumper near the pod's rear nose, keeping total chassis length around 10 meters.
